note: Event cards typed by Orbis. Dates: astronomical years (1 BC = 0); ancient dates before 45 BC follow the Roman tradition and are given as years only. Each card names its source (an ancient author and/or the Wikipedia article).

items.title: Rome is founded
items.text: Roman tradition dated the founding of the city to 753 BC. The Roman way of counting years 'from the founding of the city' (ab urbe condita, AUC) starts here; the date itself is legend, not record.
items.source: Varro's date, via Livy 1; Wikipedia 'Founding of Rome'

items.title: The Republic
items.text: Romans expelled their last king and began to elect two consuls each year. The year 509 BC is the traditional date.

items.title: Gauls sack Rome
items.text: A Gallic army beat the Romans at the Allia river and sacked the city. Livy dates it to 390 BC, Polybius to 387 BC.

items.title: First war with Carthage
items.text: Rome and Carthage fought for 23 years over Sicily, mostly at sea. Rome won and made Sicily its first province outside Italy.

items.title: Hannibal crosses the Alps
items.text: Hannibal marched an army with war elephants from Carthago Nova in Spain over the Pyrenees and the Alps into Italy. The exact pass is still debated.
items.source: Polybius 3; Wikipedia "Hannibal's crossing of the Alps"

items.title: Cannae
items.text: Hannibal encircled a much larger Roman army. Roman dead: about 48,000 according to Livy, 70,000 according to Polybius.

items.title: Zama
items.text: Scipio defeated Hannibal in Africa. Carthage gave up Spain and its fleet, and needed Rome's permission to wage war.

items.title: Carthage destroyed
items.text: After a three-year siege Rome razed Carthage and made its land the province of Africa. The same year Rome destroyed Corinth in Greece.

items.title: Pompey takes Syria
items.text: Pompey ended the Seleucid kingdom and made Syria a Roman province.

items.title: Caesar in Gaul
items.text: Julius Caesar conquered Gaul in eight years of war; the siege of Alesia in 52 BC decided it.

items.title: Caesar murdered
items.text: Senators stabbed Caesar on the Ides of March, 44 BC, after he had made himself dictator for life.
items.source: Suetonius, Divus Julius 82; Wikipedia 'Assassination of Julius Caesar'

items.title: Actium and Egypt
items.text: Octavian's fleet beat Antony and Cleopatra at Actium. A year later Egypt became a Roman province.

items.title: Augustus, first emperor
items.text: The Senate gave Octavian the name Augustus in 27 BC. Historians count the Empire from here.

items.title: Teutoburg Forest
items.text: Germanic tribes under Arminius destroyed three Roman legions. Rome gave up the land between the Rhine and the Elbe.
items.source: Cassius Dio 56; Wikipedia 'Battle of the Teutoburg Forest'

items.title: Britain invaded
items.text: Claudius sent four legions across the Channel; southern Britain became a province.
items.source: Cassius Dio 60; Wikipedia 'Roman conquest of Britain'

items.title: Dacia and Arabia
items.text: Trajan conquered Dacia (today's Romania) and annexed the Nabataean kingdom as the province of Arabia.

items.title: Trajan reaches the Gulf
items.text: Trajan took the Parthian capital Ctesiphon and reached the Persian Gulf. His successor Hadrian gave up Mesopotamia in 117.
